findings.ref: _rollback_transaction discard deferral (bundle lines 27065-27080) and step 14 post-publication branches (bundle lines 28566-28608); mutation-proofs-round7.log mutant C
findings.note: Weighed on its merits, as directed, rather than on the fact of disclosure. The round-9 change defers the journal delete to the far side of the Block Evidence write on both post-publication branches, and is the one behavioural change in the shipped bytes with zero test coverage: mutant C restores the old ordering and the suite still reports 355/0. I accept it. It is strictly fail-closed relative to what it replaces (a crash in the closed window now leaves a standing journal that the next scan classifies as its unrecoverable third state and Blocks on, instead of leaving Evidence asserting a publication whose artifacts have been rolled back with no journal to notice); it adds no fourth journal operation, only moves an existing delete; the end state is byte-identical on every non-crashing path, which is exactly why no fixture can see it; and the incomplete-rollback retention path is untouched. The disclosure is accurate and mutation-backed rather than asserted. Residual: the ordering is unproven by test and sits on a Security-Sensitive rollback path, so a future edit could silently revert it. A harness kill hook between the rollback and the Evidence write is the only thing that would lock it.
